text: The book asserts that absolute convergence of a series implies convergence, while the converse fails — a series can converge without converging absolutely.
explanation: This is exactly the book's claim: if ∑ |aₙ| converges then ∑ aₙ converges, whereas the alternating harmonic series ∑ (−1)^(n+1)/n converges conditionally — it converges even though ∑ 1/n does not. The implication therefore holds in one direction only, making the statement true.
